item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on September 24, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-24
CGTN: We’ve noted that the fifth Global Digital Trade Expo (GDTE) opened in Hangzhou this morning under the theme “Meet the AI Future at GDTE.” Premier Li Qiang attended and addressed the launching ceremony. Can you share more information on that? Guo Jiakun: This morning, the fifth GDTE opened in Hangzhou. Premier Li Qiang attended and addressed the launching ceremony. Leaders including Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim and Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers of Kyrgyzstan Adylbek Aleshovich Kasymaliev attended and addressed the launching ceremony. Other leaders including Director General of the UN Industrial Development Organization Gerd Müller addressed the event via video link. Over 1,200 representatives from various sectors of close to 50 countries and regions and relevant international organizations attended the launching ceremony. In response to questions such as where global trade is heading amid the trend of digitalization, what should the world do to capitalize on that trend, and what role can China play, Premier Li Qiang shared three observations. First, the need to grasp the new changes and new trends in global trade through digital trade. Flourishing digital trade provides new impetus and opportunities. The world economy faces broad prospects as well as new development gaps. Market matching becomes more convenient while at the same time, new trade barriers emerge. Global trade can accelerate growth through innovation, but without sufficient protection of relevant rules. Second, openness is essential to enable better development of global trade in the digital era. Amid economic globalization, the international community needs to engage in sincere coordination. We need to enhance digital connectivity for more free trade, bridge the digital divide for more universally beneficial trade, and improve digital governance for more orderly trade. Third, China will make greater contribution to global digital trade. We will keep expanding digital consumer demand and share market opportunities with countries around the world. We will continue to strengthen support for the digital industry and empower global digitalization. China’s technology advancement follows an open-source approach such as in the field of artificial intelligence to build “digital ladders” accessible to all countries. We will continue to improve the environment for digital development and offer China’s solutions to setting up well-rounded international rules. Foreign leaders noted in their remarks that the the GDTE provides an invaluable platform for countries to have discussions on cooperation, jointly promote development and share outcomes. They appreciated China’s effort of sharing development outcomes and expressed hopes to work with China to bridge the digital divide, build a fair, safe and secure global digital trade order for good and for all, and provide new impetus for the sustainable development of the world. The fifth GDTE coincides with the joyous occasion of the Mid-Autumn Festival. We welcome friends from the press to cover this event and feel the vibe of cutting-edge technology in Hangzhou. Reuters: The U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said that the U.S. and China have reached a deal to extend the current trade truce all the way to January 10. China has so far not released any information about this. Has China agreed to this two-month extension? Guo Jiakun: I’d refer you to competent authorities for any specifics regarding the China-U.S. consultations on economic and trade issues. Bloomberg: The Iranian president said during a UN address that his country won’t allow freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz while sanctions and a U.S. blockade remain in place. We’re wondering if the foreign ministry has any comment on his remarks. Guo Jiakun: Protraction of the U.S.-Iran conflict does not serve the common interests of the parties concerned or the international community. It is vital for parties to choose peace, resolve disputes through dialogue and negotiation, and restore peace and tranquility to the Middle East and Gulf region at an early date. The New York Times: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said that China and the U.S. agreed to set up a formalized dialogue on AI that includes an incident line for communicating about AI safety incidents. Can MOFA confirm whether China has agreed to this dialogue and this notification system? Guo Jiakun: The Chinese side has released a readout on the China-U.S. consultations on economic and trade issues, which you may refer to. For further information, I’d refer you to competent authorities. NHK: It has been almost a month since Gyirong County was hit by the devastating mudslide. Could you provide the latest casualty figures for foreign nationals and an update on the rescue operations? Guo Jiakun: The disaster left 261 foreign nationals unaccounted for. China has shared information with their countries’ embassies in Beijing. Reuters: New Zealand’s cyber security agency said China was the country’s most persistent and capable state-backed cyber threat. What is the ministry’s comment of this? Guo Jiakun: China opposes and resolutely fights hacker attacks in accordance with law, and opposes the dissemination of cyber security disinformation for political purposes. China urges the relevant agency in New Zealand to stop spreading lies and stoking discord, and instead do more to foster mutual understanding and trust between the two countries. The New York Times: Are further trade talks planned between the United States and China on the sidelines of the APEC finance ministers’ meeting in Hong Kong in October, or in conjunction with the APEC summit in Shenzhen? Has China formally invited Mr. Trump to the Shenzhen summit? Guo Jiakun: On questions related to the China-U.S. consultations on economic and trade issues, I’d refer you to competent authorities. On your second question, China and the U.S. are in communication regarding interactions between the two presidents within the year. ******************************************************** During the Mid-Autumn Festival, there will be no regular press conference on September 25. The regular press conference will resume on September 28. During this period, questions can be submitted to the Spokesperson’s Office via fax, E-mail or WeChat. We wish you and your family a happy Mid-Autumn Festival!

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on September 23, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-23
CCTV: The 48th WorldSkills Competition is being held in Shanghai. President Xi Jinping sent a congratulatory letter to the event. This morning, Premier Li Qiang attended and addressed the opening ceremony of the WorldSkills Conference. The WorldSkills Expo is also being held at the same time. Can you provide more information on these events? Guo Jiakun: The 48th WorldSkills Competition has kicked off in Shanghai, bringing together a record number of nearly 1,400 competitors from 68 countries and regions. President Xi Jinping sent a congratulatory letter to the WorldSkills Competition. He noted that a new round of scientific and technological revolution and industrial transformation is advancing rapidly, exerting a profound impact on global skills development. China will take the opportunity of hosting this year’s competition to encourage and guide more workers, especially young people, to pursue a path to success through skills. China is willing to strengthen exchanges and cooperation with all parties, promote the development of the WorldSkills movement, and better contribute to global economic growth and the improvement of people’s well-being. Premier Li Qiang attended and addressed the opening ceremony of the WorldSkills Conference. He noted that skills have always been an important force driving the progress of human civilization, and that skills have made significant contributions to China’s development. As China is now building a modern industrial system, the mutual reinforcement of talents and skills is providing an inexhaustible source of energy for the country’s high-quality development. Traditional Chinese skills and craftsmanship have been passed down from generation to generation, with many reaching the rest of the world. They have not only contributed to talent development and industrial growth in various countries, but also helped build close ties among civilizations. China has always been committed to strengthening the skills of the workforce, with a focus on integration between industries and skills, lifelong vocational education and training, and a culture that encourages people to pursue success through skills. All parties should work together to create a bright future for skills development. It is important to develop skills that are more responsive to people’s needs and invest more in people; to develop skills with greater innovative vitality and take a forward-looking approach to cultivating highly skilled talents; and to develop more open and inclusive skills by establishing closer mechanisms for international exchanges and cooperation on skills and building an open ecosystem for skills. China is ready to join all parties to build the global skills innovation center, and strengthen skills development under the Belt and Road Initiative and through South-South cooperation. Premier Li Qiang also toured the WorldSkills Expo. Prime Minister of Malaysia Anwar Ibrahim and President of WorldSkills International Francis Hourant attended the opening ceremony of the WorldSkills Conference. In their remarks, they spoke highly of China’s important contributions to global skills development and youth development, and expressed readiness to enhance exchanges and mutual learning with China to make skills an important bond for win-win cooperation. Amid the volatile international situation, China will stay committed to skills and talent development to empower economic and social progress, and continue to make China’s contributions to global skills development. The WorldSkills Competition will last until September 27. Journalists are welcome to cover the event. Reuters: Are you able to confirm whether President Xi will be accompanied by a delegation of Chinese executives when he travels to Washington later this week? There have been mixed reports in the media. Guo Jiakun: I have no information to share. CCTV: On September 22 local time, Prime Minister of Japan Sanae Takaichi said at the UN General Assembly that Japan has consistently contributed to the peace and prosperity of the international community as a peace-loving nation, under its exclusively defense-oriented policy. It is Japan’s mission to lead the efforts of the international community towards a “world without nuclear weapons.” The “Enemy State Clauses” must be deleted. What’s your comment? Guo Jiakun: Rather than what Japan says, the world cares more about what Japan does. The postwar “country for peace” image that Japan seeks to establish can only be realized by repenting its history and making a clean break with militarism. The reality with the current Japanese administration, however, is a constant denial of the history of aggression, glorification of Japan’s wartime crimes, and a series of moves to rearm Japan, accelerate remilitarization, seek to ditch the three non-nuclear principles, and revise the pacifist Constitution. The moves constitute a blatant challenge to the postwar international order, and a major factor threatening peace and stability in the region. This year marks the 81st anniversary of the founding of the UN, and the 80th anniversary of the opening of the Tokyo Trials. Decades ago, Japan joined the UN after recognizing its militarist crimes and accepting the UN Charter in its entirety. The “Enemy State Clauses” in the UN Charter are a vital institutional arrangement aimed at preventing fascism and militarism from threatening international peace and security ever again. The clauses provide important institutional safeguards for defending postwar international order and remain extremely relevant today. We urge Japan to take history as a mirror, deeply repent, and earn the trust of its Asian neighbors and the international community through concrete actions. AFP: The U.S. has threatened to punish countries that allow Iranian flights to land on their territory from today. Can I ask if China will keep receiving and accommodating flights from Tehran? Guo Jiakun: China’s position has been consistent. We firmly oppose illicit unilateral sanctions that have no basis in international law and lack UN Security Council mandate.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on September 22, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-22
Vice President Han Zheng will attend the general debate of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York from September 24 to 26. On the sidelines of the general debate, Vice President Han will attend the High-Level Dialogue on the Fifth Anniversary of the Global Development Initiative hosted by China, and meet with UN Secretary-General, President of the 81st UNGA session, and leaders of relevant countries. The 48th WorldSkills Competition will be held in Shanghai from September 22 to 27. The fifth Global Digital Trade Expo will be held in Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province from September 23 to 27. At China’s invitation, Prime Minister of Malaysia Anwar Ibrahim will attend the opening ceremony of the WorldSkills Competition and the launching ceremony of the Global Digital Trade Expo, and Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers of Kyrgyzstan Adylbek Aleshovich Kasymaliev will attend the launching ceremony of the Global Digital Trade Expo. CCTV: You just announced that Vice President Han Zheng will attend the general debate of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly. What is China’s expectation for his trip? Guo Jiakun: Across the world, changes unseen in a century are accelerating. The international landscape is volatile and fraught with risks and challenges. The United Nations is the core platform for global governance, and the general debate of UNGA is a vital opportunity for countries to build political consensus and coordinate multilateral actions. This year marks the 55th anniversary of the restoration of the People’s Republic of China’s lawful seat in the UN. At the general debate, Vice President Han Zheng will present China’s views and propositions on the current international landscape, major international and regional issues, and the work of the UN. He will outline China’s strong actions to advance true multilateralism and promote world peace and development, and call on the international community to revitalize the authority and role of the UN, build greater synergy for reforming and improving global governance, and work together in the right direction of building a community with a shared future for humanity. The Paper: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim will attend two major events hosted by China. What’s China’s comment on the current relations with Malaysia? What is your expectation for the prime minister’s visit? Guo Jiakun: China and Malaysia are good neighbors, good friends and good partners connected by sea. Over the past 50 plus years of diplomatic relations, bilateral ties have maintained sound momentum of growth with good progress in cooperation across the board. The two countries are jointly building a high-level strategic community with a shared future. Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim’s attendance at events of the WorldSkills Competition and the Global Digital Trade Expo demonstrates the two countries’ close and warm ties and sound cooperation in relevant areas. China looks forward to working with Malaysia to further synergize development strategies, promote high-quality Belt and Road cooperation, have close communication and coordination on international and regional issues, and strive for more outcomes in building the high-level strategic China-Malaysia community with a shared future. AFP: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned on Monday that Iranian airlines will have trouble functioning globally under the weight of American sanctions. He said in an interview that tomorrow, all the Iranian airlines will be shut down around the world, and that countries that provide these airlines with landing services or fuel would be knocked out of the dollar system. Can the foreign ministry comment on this since there seems to be Iranian airlines flights landing in Guangzhou and Shanghai tomorrow morning? Will China accommodate these Iranian flights? Guo Jiakun: China opposes illicit unilateral sanctions that have no basis in international law and lack UN Security Council mandate. Sky News: At the weekend, He Lifeng was meeting with a delegation from the U.S. and afterwards Scott Bessent told the press that the two negotiating teams had discussed establishing an AI dialogue. There were also reports about a possible notification mechanism of AI incidents between the U.S. and China. Can we expect specific measures on AI to be announced at the leaders’ summit that we expect to happen this week? Does China believe that these overtures from the U.S. are being made in good faith, or is there a belief that there is a desire from the U.S. to curtail China’s AI rise? Guo Jiakun: The Chinese side has released a readout regarding the China-U.S. consultations on economic and trade issues. I’d refer you to competent authorities for the specific questions. CGTN: Yesterday, the 23rd China-ASEAN Expo concluded successfully, yielding fruitful outcomes. Last week, the Pinglu Canal officially opened to navigation, which received extensive public attention both in China and abroad. Some call the China-ASEAN Expo a “Golden Platform” and the Pinglu Canal a “Golden Waterway,” and believe that they will open a new chapter of China-ASEAN cooperation. What’s your comment? Guo Jiakun: The China-ASEAN Expo is a shining brand of China-ASEAN cooperation. Over the past 23 years, the Expo witnessed China-ASEAN cooperation leaping through the “Golden Decade” to the “Diamond Decade” and the upgrade to the China-ASEAN Free Trade Area 3.0 (CAFTA 3.0). This year, for the very first time, the Expo designated an area tailored to ASEAN countries’ demand and released an ASEAN countries’ demand list aimed at precision matchmaking between what ASEAN needs and what China can provide. The Expo also designated a Pinglu Canal exhibition area. The Canal’s opening to navigation will significantly reduce the maritime shipping distance from Southwest China to ASEAN countries, opening up a new route for bilateral trade. China is ready to work with ASEAN countries to implement CAFTA 3.0 and build an even closer China-ASEAN community with a shared future. NHK: The Foreign Ministry Spokesperson’s Office today posted a video titled “Constructive Strategic Stability” on its social media account. What is China’s consideration and purpose of posting the video? As President Xi Jinping is set to pay a state visit to the United States, what message does China hope to convey to the U.S. and the international community through the video? Guo Jiakun: We appreciate your interest in the Foreign Ministry’s social media account. China is ready to work with the U.S. to enrich the China-U.S. constructive relationship of strategic stability, enhance dialogue and cooperation, and properly manage differences to contribute to the well-being of both peoples and to a peaceful, stable and prosperous world. Sky News: Returning to the issue of AI governance, which is gonna be such an important topic probably between President Xi and President Trump this week. I wonder if China has any further comments in response to a lot of the commentary we’ve seen over the weekend about how important this issue of working together on governance is and any intentions going into that summit. Guo Jiakun: China has made clear on multiple occasions its position on issues related to AI. Parties need to work together for the open and inclusive development of AI for all and for good.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on September 21, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-21
Xinhua News Agency: China just announced President Xi’s state visit to the United States. Could you please share more information about the schedule and China’s expectation for China-U.S. relations? Guo Jiakun: At the invitation of President Donald J. Trump, President Xi Jinping will soon pay a state visit to the United States. During his visit, President Xi will have an in-depth exchange of views with President Trump on major issues concerning bilateral ties and world peace and development. Head-of-state diplomacy plays an irreplaceable role in providing strategic guidance to China-U.S. relations. The exchange of visits by the two presidents within the span of half a year will mark a milestone of historic significance. China will work with the United States to enrich the dimensions of the China-U.S. constructive relationship of strategic stability, strengthen dialogue and cooperation, and properly manage differences, so as to deliver greater benefits to our two peoples and further contribute to world peace, stability and prosperity. China News Agency: On the fifth anniversary of the Global Development Initiative (GDI) put forward by President Xi Jinping, could you update us on the implementation of the initiative over the past five years? Is China considering hosting events on the initiative on the sidelines of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly? Guo Jiakun: Five years ago today, President Xi Jinping put forward the GDI at the general debate of the 76th session of the UN General Assembly. Focusing on development, a timeless theme for humanity, the initiative pools together international efforts to put development high on the global macro policy agenda, aims to expedite the implementation of the UN 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, and has injected strong impetus into revitalizing global development. The initiative has received extensive recognition from the international community. Over the past five years, under the guidance of President Xi Jinping and with the joint effort of various parties, fruitful outcomes have been made in implementing the GDI. The GDI has turned from a Chinese proposal into a global consensus, with people-centered development philosophy enjoying increasing popularity. The GDI has played a greater role in driving global development by real actions. Under the framework of the initiative, more than US$23 billion have been mobilized, and more than 2,000 cooperation projects have been carried out. In particular, practical cooperation under the framework of the Global Development and South-South Cooperation Fund has yielded fruitful outcomes in 70 plus countries, benefiting more than 40 million people. The GDI has developed better cooperation architecture across various sectors, laying the groundwork for advancing international development cooperation as well as realizing UN Sustainable Development Goals. The general debate of the 81st session of the General Assembly starts tomorrow. On the sidelines of the general debate, China will host the High-Level Dialogue on the Fifth Anniversary of the Global Development Initiative at the UN headquarters in New York on September 25. We look forward to working with the broader UN membership to take stock of the achievements and useful experiences over the past five years, share development opportunities, explore cooperation on development, facilitate the implementation of the UN 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, and build a community with a shared future for humanity. The New York Times: A U.S. official said last week at a briefing that China has not fully resumed rare earth deliveries despite agreeing to do so at previous summits of the two leaders. What is China’s position? Guo Jiakun: I’d refer you to competent authorities for the specific question. China is committed to keeping the global industrial and supply chains of critical minerals safe and stable. China and the United States should jointly implement the important common understandings reached between the two presidents and maintain the steady growth momentum of China-U.S. economic and trade ties. Shenzhen TV: Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson stated on September 18 that Russia had sent a note of protest to the Japanese side regarding the deployment of Typhon missile systems on Kyushu Island. The Kremlin considers the deployment unacceptable and demanded that the Japanese side fully recognize the results of WWII and abandon its remilitarization policy. China also recently sent a note to the Japanese side to express its concerns. Can you confirm that and share more details on that? Guo Jiakun: The deployment of Typhon missile system, a strategic offensive weapon, is yet another example of Japan’s accelerated remilitarization. Such move will only push up the risk of military confrontation and arms race, threaten strategic balance and regional stability, and harm the legitimate security interests of neighboring countries. The international community is on high alert, with people from multiple Asian countries voicing their opposition to the deployment. China has also lodged strong protests against Japan through diplomatic channels on multiple occasions, and has recently sent a diplomatic note to Japan to reiterate China’s solemn position. On the occasion of the 80th anniversary of the opening of the Tokyo Trials, China urges Japan to do serious soul-searching on its history of aggression, face up to the call from regional countries, and stop advancing its remilitarization agenda. Reuters: The New Zealand Defence Force said today that two of its naval ships have transited the Taiwan Strait. The New Zealand PM called this a routine activity and said he was not expecting any backlash from China. Does China have any comment on this event? Guo Jiakun: China’s position on foreign military vessels’ transit through the Taiwan Strait is consistent. Beijing Youth Daily: According to preliminary results, the United Russia Party is leading in Russia’s State Duma elections held from September 18 to 20. What’s China’s comment? Guo Jiakun: China extends congratulations over the smooth conclusion of the Russian State Duma elections. The elections are a major event on Russia’s political calendar. The results of the elections represent the will of the Russian people. As a friendly neighbor and comprehensive strategic partner of coordination for a new era, China firmly supports the Russian people’s independent choice and stands ready to continue working with the Russian side to act on the important common understandings between the two presidents to make fresh progress and bring bilateral relations to new heights. The New York Times: Is China amenable to an extension of the November 10 deadline for expanded restrictions on rare earth exports, and if so, for how long? Guo Jiakun: I’d refer you to competent authorities for anything specific. China Daily: It’s reported that a terrorist attack on a police facility in Pakistan’s Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province on September 18 caused heavy casualties. Does China have a comment? Guo Jiakun: China strongly condemns this attack. We mourn for the loss of lives and extend sincere sympathies to the injured and the bereaved families. Terrorism is a common enemy of humanity. Fighting terrorism is in the shared interests of all countries. China will continue its steadfast support for Pakistan’s counter-terrorism efforts. We call on all countries to join forces in tackling the threat of terrorism and safeguard global security and stability. The New York Times: China’s restrictions this year on rare earth exports to Japan have affected American supply chains. Will this also be discussed at the summit later this week in Washington? Guo Jiakun: I’ve just shared relevant information on the summit. On the rare earth exports restriction you mentioned, in accordance with laws and regulations, China prohibits the export of all dual-use items to Japanese military users and for Japan’s military use, and any export that could help enhance Japan’s military capabilities. The aim is to thwart Japan’s remilitarization and attempt to possess nuclear weapons. China’s position of keeping the global industrial and supply chains of critical minerals safe and stable has not changed. All parties have the responsibility to play a constructive role to this end. The New York Times: Do you have any further details regarding what progress may have been made in the conversations in New York City between Vice Premier He Lifeng and Treasury Secretary Bessent? Guo Jiakun: The Chinese side has released a readout, which you may refer to. I have no further information to offer. The New York Times: CNN reported at the end of last week that the U.S. military had been falsely responding to an AI report that a Chinese vessel was moving military components to the Middle East. Do you have any comment on this? Guo Jiakun: I am not aware of what you mentioned.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on September 18, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-18
CGTN: This year marks the 95th anniversary of the September 18 Incident. Quite a few Japanese media and scholars have warned that the security policies of the Sanae Takaichi administration are showing a dangerous tendency of reversing to the prewar path, that the Japanese society is suffering a dismissive attitude toward war, and that modern Japan is heading down a path similar to that of the 1930s and needs to correct course at once. What is China’s comment? Guo Jiakun: Ninety-five years ago today, Japanese militarists launched the aggression against China. They were met by the courageous resistance of the Chinese people. It lifted the curtain of the eastern theater of the World Anti-Fascist War. The September 18 Incident was a war plot long concealed by the Japanese government to the Japanese public. The vast majority of the Japanese people did not learn the truth until the Tokyo Trials, which opened exactly 80 years ago. The increasingly prevalent historical denialism in Japan is truly troubling and the danger is self-evident. Even today, Japanese textbooks continue to downplay the nature of Japan’s aggression, and right-wing forces in Japan even use artificial intelligence to systemically filter prewar archives and records of the Tokyo Trials, in an attempt to whitewash Japan’s war crimes and entrench a distorted view of history. Denialism not just reflects serious regression in Japan’s perception of history, but also indicates alarmingly an organized attempt to turn back the wheel of history with clear political motives. The real purpose is to keep the Japanese public from the truth, and clear the path for Japan to escape the straitjacket of the postwar system and rearm itself. To deny the crimes of aggression is to challenge the verdict of history and tear down the postwar international order. We urge the Japanese side to face up to and repent for its history of aggression, and earn the trust of its Asian neighbors and the wider international community through concrete actions. It is absolutely essential for China and all other countries in the region to stay on high alert. Japanese militarism must never be revived, and the tragedies of history must never be repeated. We must work together to uphold the outcomes of the World War II victory and jointly safeguard peace. Bloomberg: We’re wondering if President Xi will be going to the U.S.? If so, which day will he be going? Guo Jiakun: China and the U.S. are in communication regarding interactions between the two heads of state within the year. RIA Novosti: The European Union has asked Chinese authorities to voluntarily cap Chinese hybrid vehicles sales at around 15 percent of the bloc’s market to avoid a trade war. Would the foreign ministry like to comment on this? Guo Jiakun: I’d refer you to competent authorities for anything specific. Let me stress that China-EU economic and trade relations are mutually beneficial in nature, not a zero-sum competition. Engaging in open cooperation and resolving economic and trade disputes through equal-footed dialogue and consultation serve the common interests of both sides. The development of China’s EV industry provides quality and affordable products for global consumers and contributes to global green and low-carbon transition. We hope the EU will honor its commitments to market openness and free trade, observe WTO rules, and provide a fair, just and non-discriminatory environment for companies of all countries. We will closely follow the EU’s moves and do what is necessary to protect the legitimate and lawful rights and interests of our businesses. CCTV: It is reported that the National Cultural Heritage Administration of China received 64 pieces of Chinese cultural relics and fossils returned by the Homeland Security Investigations of the United States and Manhattan District Attorney’s Office in Washington and New York on Wednesday and Thursday local time respectively. These antiquities are discovered by the U.S. law enforcement authorities. Could you share more details on that? What’s China’s comment? Guo Jiakun: Since China and the U.S. signed the intergovernmental memorandum of understanding on preventing the illegal entry of Chinese cultural relics into the U.S., our practical cooperation has yielded fruitful outcomes, evidenced by the returning of a total of 700 plus pieces of Chinese cultural relics and art works lost in the U.S. in 20 plus batches. The repatriation marks the latest step to implement the common understandings reached by the two presidents in their meetings in Beijing, and also demonstrates the broad prospects of building a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability. China and the U.S. should go toward the same direction in the spirit of equality, mutual respect and mutual benefit so as to accomplish more great and concrete things for the good of our two countries and peoples. AFP: The Philippine Coast Guard said that on Friday morning, a China Coast Guard vessel rammed a Philippine boat near Sabina Shoal, known in Chinese as Xianbin Jiao. We have seen the statement just released by the China Coast Guard. Does the foreign ministry have any specific comments to address to the Philippines regarding this incident? Guo Jiakun: As you said, China Coast Guard spokesperson has made a statement to share information on the real situation. This morning, an official vessel from the Philippines started provocations and deliberately rammed at the China Coast Guard vessel in the adjacent waters of Xianbin Jiao, Nansha Qundao. Such moves pose a serious threat to the safety of China’s personnel and vessels, and constitute a serious violation of the international law and basic norms governing international relations. The Philippines should immediately stop its infringement activities at sea, and stop spreading false narratives and disinformation. China will continue safeguarding its territorial sovereignty and maritime rights and interests, and keeping the South China Sea peaceful and stable.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on September 17, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-17
Phoenix TV: The Global Financial Centres Index 40 Report was published yesterday. Hong Kong’s overall ranking maintained third place globally and first place in Asia Pacific. What’s your comment? Guo Jiakun: With the safeguards of One Country, Two Systems, Hong Kong has witnessed remarkable economic growth. Its leading position as an international financial, shipping and trade center has been further reaffirmed. Hong Kong’s IPO market in the first half of the year had come in second globally, raising around HK$ 203.3 billion. The report reaffirms Hong Kong’s appeal, influence and competitiveness as an international financial hub. It represents yet another vote of confidence in Hong Kong’s unique status and strengths and in the prospects of One Country, Two Systems. Telesur: Yesterday, here in Beijing, Foreign Minister Wang Yi met with Celso Amorim, the Chief Advisor to President Lula, who delivered a letter from the Brazilian president to President Xi Jinping. How does the Chinese government assess the message in the letter? And has the Chinese side responded or sent any message to President Lula? Guo Jiakun: In recent years, under the strategic guidance of the two presidents, China-Brazil relations have been growing by leaps and bounds, evolving from comprehensive strategic partnership to a community with a shared future. President Xi Jinping and President Lula are in close communication via various ways, demonstrating the high-level political mutual trust between our two countries. Telesur: I have another question related to the meeting between Wang Yi and Celso Amorim. The two sides also discussed the situation in Latin America. The United States has recently increased the pressure against Brazil, including criticism of its handling of organized crimes and discussions about possible new sanctions against Brazilian Supreme Court justices, as Brazil approaches its 2026 presidential election. How does China view these developments, particularly regarding respect for Brazil’s sovereignty and its electoral process? Guo Jiakun: China adheres to non-interference in other countries’ internal affairs. We wish Brazil a steady and smooth election. Beijing Daily: We noticed that on the sidelines of the 63rd session of the Human Rights Council, the Chinese side and the UN Office at Geneva co-hosted an exhibition themed “Accessibility for All” at the Palais des Nations in Geneva. Can you provide more information about the event? Guo Jiakun: The exhibition brought together more than 300 guests, including UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk, permanent representatives of various countries, heads of international organizations, and media representatives. The exhibition offered a comprehensive look at China’s practices in advancing “accessibility for all” in areas such as technology, culture, employment and the rule of law. The event was warmly received with guests trying out cutting-edge smart assistive devices and viewing artworks by persons with disabilities. Building a barrier-free environment is an important part of human rights protection. In October 2024, the 57th session of the Human Rights Council adopted by consensus a resolution proposed by China, on behalf of 30 countries, titled “Promoting accessibility for the full enjoyment of all human rights by all”. Holding this exhibition is an important step in implementing that resolution. This year marks the first anniversary of the Global Governance Initiative proposed by President Xi Jinping and the third anniversary of the implementation of the Law of the People’s Republic of China on the Building of a Barrier-free Environment. China will once again propose a resolution on accessibility to this session of the Human Rights Council. We stand ready to work with the international community to further enrich practices in human rights protection, improve global human rights governance, and together build a community with a shared future for humanity. Bloomberg: The U.S. Congress gave final approval to a bill to give President Donald Trump new powers to impose tariffs on countries that purchase Russian petroleum products. We are wondering if the foreign ministry has any comments? Guo Jiakun: China engages in normal economic and trade cooperation with other countries on the basis of equality and mutual benefit. Such cooperation does not target any third party and shall be free from disruption or coercion from any third party. China opposes long-arm jurisdiction and unilateral sanctions that have no basis in international law and lack UN Security Council mandate.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on September 16, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-16
Member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Vice Premier of the State Council Ding Xuexiang will attend and address the Opening Ceremony of the 23rd China-ASEAN Expo and China-ASEAN Business and Investment Summit to be held in Nanning, Guangxi on September 17. Vice President of Myanmar U Nyo Saw, Politburo Member of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of Viet Nam and Standing Deputy Prime Minister Pham Gia Tuc, and Politburo Member of the Central Committee of the Lao’s People’s Revolutionary Party, Deputy Prime Minister and Standing Member of the Cabinet Saleumxay Kommasith, among other foreign leaders and senior officials, and Secretary-General of ASEAN Kao Kim Hourn will attend the Opening Ceremony. People’s Daily: What is China’s expectation for the 23rd China-ASEAN Expo and China-ASEAN Business and Investment Summit? Guo Jiakun: The State Council Information Office has held a briefing on September 1 to share detailed information about the 23rd China-ASEAN Expo and China-ASEAN Business and Investment Summit. This year marks the fifth anniversary of the China-ASEAN comprehensive strategic partnership. Under the strategic guidance of leaders of both sides, China and ASEAN have engaged in fruitful practical cooperation in various areas and built increasingly closer economic and trade ties. China stands ready to work with ASEAN countries and make full use of the platforms of the China-ASEAN Expo and China-ASEAN Business and Investment Summit to further unleash cooperation potential in various fields, achieve mutual benefit at a higher level, and build an even closer China-ASEAN community with a shared future. Kyodo News: Today, dozens of descendants of Chinese forced laborers in WWII filed a lawsuit against several Japanese companies with Hebei High People’s Court. What’s your comment? Guo Jiakun: The forced recruitment and enslavement of laborers is one of the serious crimes committed by Japanese militarists during their foreign aggression and colonial rule. China urges Japan to look history in the eye, reflect on past crimes, earnestly heed and respond to the just calls and legitimate claims of the people of victim countries in Asia, and properly resolve relevant issues left over from history with a responsible attitude. Xinhua News Agency: It’s reported that the EU telecom lobby Connect Europe issued an open letter yesterday, saying that the revised Cybersecurity Act (CSA) “risks draining the sector of the very capital needed for fibre, 5G and 6G. The blanket equipment removal requirements foreseen by the CSA would impose up to €40 billion in replacement costs on our sector.” The letter was signed by 17 top European telecom companies’ executives, including the CEOs of France’s Orange, Germany’s Deutsche Telekom and Spain’s Telefonica. What’s your comment? Guo Jiakun: China noticed relevant reports. According to the assessment by relevant institutions, the Act will possibly cause loss of up to over €360 billion in the EU within the next five years. The open letter by the European telecommunication companies is yet another example that the EU’s moves will only hurt others while bringing no benefits to its own. Protectionism does not build competitiveness, but destroys EU opportunities for digital transformation, harms EU’s socioeconomic development, tarnishes its open-market reputation, and dampens foreign companies’ confidence in investing in the EU. We hope the EU will heed the voice of reason across various sectors and not adopt discriminatory restrictions. Global Times: It is reported that Lin Chia-lung, head of the “foreign affairs” department of the Taiwan authorities, in a recent interview confirmed the plan to set up a “representative’s office” in the central Philippine province of Cebu, which will serve as a platform to deepen ties through the “Taiwan-Philippines economic corridor.” What’s your comment? Guo Jiakun: Let me stress again, no matter how the DPP authorities collude with external forces to seek “diplomatic breakthroughs” and advance their separatist agenda in whatever form, such attempts will be all in vain and doomed to fail. We also urge the Philippine side to abide by the one-China principle with concrete actions, and refrain from taking any steps that could harm China-Philippines relations.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson’s Remarks on Japanese Politicians Paying Respects to the Yasukuni War Shrine Which Honors Class-A War Criminals
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-15
Q: August 15 marks the day of Japan’s unconditional surrender in the Second World War. Prime Minister of Japan Sanae Takaichi made a monetary offering to the Yasukuni war shrine today, and certain cabinet members also visited the shrine. What’s your comment? A: China strongly deplores Japan’s negative moves related to the Yasukuni war shrine, and has lodged serious protests against Japan. During WWII, Japan launched the war of aggression and committed horrendous crimes. The Yasukuni war shrine is a spiritual tool and symbol of Japanese militarism. It is in fact a shrine for war criminals, as it honors 14 convicted Class-A war criminals responsible for the war of aggression. No pretext whatsoever can hide the Japanese politicians’ true intention which is to change the verdict on the war criminals, cover up Japan’s war crimes, distort the historical facts, and pave the way for accelerating remilitarization. This is an affront to historical justice, a challenge to the foundational norms of civilization, and a provocation against the postwar international order. Such behaviors have been firmly rejected by the overwhelming majority of the international community. This year marks the 80th anniversary of the opening of the Tokyo Trials. To view and treat history correctly is an important prerequisite for Japan’s postwar return to the international community, the political foundation for Japan’s ties with neighboring countries, and more importantly, a key measure for Japan’s commitment to peaceful development. We urge the Japanese side to do serious soul-searching on its history of aggression, make a clean break with militarism, and earn trust from its Asian neighbors and the rest of the world with concrete actions.
